description:
Swinton Castle — known on Booking.com and to most of the hospitality trade by its actual name, Swinton Park — stands within a 20,000-acre estate near Masham in North Yorkshire, on the edge of the Yorkshire Dales. Its origins are considerably less dramatic than its present appearance suggests: the house was built in 1695 by Sir Abstrupus Danby, a wool merchant and Yorkshire Justice of the Peace, as a straightforward five-bay, three-storey Georgian country house, entirely without battlements, towers or any castle-like styling whatsoever.

That transformation came in two distinct phases spanning more than a century. William Danby undertook a near-total rebuilding of the house in the Gothic Revival style toward the end of the 18th century, giving the building its first genuinely castle-influenced character. But the specific features most visitors associate with Swinton today — its battlements, decorative turrets and the great round tower that dominates its skyline — were not added until the early 19th century, meaning the 'castle' identity of the building is a full century younger than its original Georgian construction, layered on in stages rather than conceived from the outset.

The estate passed into the hands of the Cunliffe-Lister family in the 1880s, and it has remained their ancestral seat ever since, today associated with the title Earl of Swinton. Samuel Cunliffe-Lister left a particularly significant architectural mark on the house, adding a complete second storey, raising the height of the tower, and constructing the palatial dining room wing that remains one of the building's grandest interior spaces — work that pushed Swinton's scale and grandeur well beyond what either Sir Abstrupus Danby or William Danby had originally built.

Swinton's identity as a hotel is a genuinely recent chapter in this long family history. Mark Cunliffe-Lister and his family bought back the estate in 2000, and rather than a slow, incremental conversion, they transformed the house into a luxury castle hotel within just nine months, opening for business in 2001. The property holds Grade II* listed status, and today offers 32 individually designed bedrooms, each themed on a different Yorkshire town, dale, garden, castle or abbey — a distinctly regional approach to interior design that ties every room back to the surrounding North Yorkshire landscape.

For day visitors, the Castle Bar is explicitly open to both hotel guests and non-residents, and the Terrace Restaurant & Bar opens daily from 10am, serving tea and coffee with garden seating available. Afternoon tea is served Monday to Saturday from noon to 5pm, and on Sundays from 3pm, with access included to the estate's 200 acres of gardens and parkland — a genuinely substantial outdoor component to what might otherwise be a simple hotel dining visit. Set on the edge of the Yorkshire Dales National Park, within reach of Fountains Abbey and the historic town of Ripon, Swinton offers visitors a chance to explore two centuries of Gothic Revival transformation within a single, still-working country estate.

The Swinton Estate itself extends well beyond the hotel building, encompassing working farmland, woodland and moorland typical of the North Yorkshire landscape, and the Cunliffe-Lister family continues to manage the wider estate as a genuine agricultural and sporting concern alongside its hospitality operation. This working-estate character distinguishes Swinton from castle-hotels that occupy only a house and immediate grounds, giving visitors a sense of the full scale of land a family of this standing would historically have controlled — a scale that also supports the estate's own cookery school, housed in a restored Georgian stable wing and using produce grown in the estate's own four-acre walled garden, alongside country pursuits including game shooting, river fishing and pony trekking across the wider grounds.

faqs.question: Is 'Swinton Castle' the same as 'Swinton Park'?
faqs.answer: Yes — Swinton Park is the property's real name, and it's the name used on Booking.com and by the hospitality trade generally. This site uses 'Swinton Castle' to match the original naming used in earlier sourcing, but Swinton Park is the correct and current name of the hotel and estate.

faqs.question: Can I visit Swinton Castle's Castle Bar without staying overnight?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Castle Bar is explicitly open to both hotel guests and non-residents, and the Terrace Restaurant & Bar opens daily from 10am with garden seating. Afternoon tea is served Monday to Saturday from noon to 5pm and Sundays from 3pm, with access included to the estate's 200 acres of gardens and parkland.

faqs.question: Is Swinton Castle a genuine medieval castle?
faqs.answer: No. The house was originally built in 1695 as a plain Georgian country house with no castle-like features. It was rebuilt in Gothic Revival style by William Danby in the late 18th century, and the battlements, turrets and great round tower that give it its present castle appearance were added only in the early 19th century — the building's 'castle' identity is a later architectural layer, not an original defensive structure.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** near Masham, North Yorkshire — note the real Booking.com/property name is 'Swinton Park.'

**Rooms & rates:** 32 rooms across the ground, first and second floors of the Castle building, including the Turret Signature Suite inside the main tower; further rooms, including a fully accessible ground-floor room, are in the separate Coach House.

**On-site:** Restaurant, Castle Bar, spa, gardens.

**Good to know:** Specify a Castle-building room (or the Turret Suite specifically) if sleeping inside the historic tower matters — the Coach House rooms are comfortable but a separate building.

**Combine with:** Fountains Abbey and Studley Royal, both within easy reach.
